Synopsis:
You find a contemplative Astarion thinking about the danger we pose if we turn into mind flayers. He asks - hypothetically - if he had to kill us, how would we like to go? As an experienced murderer, he considers it a professional courtesy, but we might be outraged. He'll be enthusiastic when describing the different ways people can die - a fan talking about his favourite subject. If we threaten him, he'll be defensive and a little sulky.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_Night2_CRD_Astarion.json: You're in camp amid rising fear that the tadpole infection is turning party members into mind flayers — others have shown signs and tensions (Lae'zel in particular is primed to react violently). Astarion has slipped into a quiet, intimate mood (he may be tracing his scars and opening up to those he trusts) and is musing on the grim possibility of stopping a transformed companion. As a practiced killer he treats the subject with grim professional curiosity and is almost gleeful when describing methods of death, framing mercy dispatch as a "professional courtesy." He speaks lightly but seriously about the danger; if you threaten or scold him he becomes defensive and a bit sulky.
- Astarion_Recruitment.json: Following a trail of whispered ADs ('Psst. Over here!' 'Come on, before it's too late!') we find a pale elf, hunched down near some long grass. He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.
- CAMP_AstarionHunger_SCO_Companion.json: You wake up and find Astarion hunching over you, fangs bared. You fight him off. Caught off guard, he's alarmed and worried that you're going to kill him. He tries to be charming, explaining that he's too weak without blood. If you push back against his excuses he gets frustrated - he tries to bargain with you. If you agree to let him bite you, he's thrilled. He feels in control again. After drinking, he feels invigorated and cocky.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_SD_ROM_NightWithAstarion.json: After the goblin hunt celebration party (whether the player helped the goblins or the tieflings), Astarion has made arrangements to get intimate with the player at night. For Astarion, this is a game of power - one he's played many times before in the taverns of Baldur's Gate, trying to lure people back to his master. He's an old hand at seduction, very self-assured at first, but the player might not go along with the script he expects them to follow. The next morning, the player wakes to see Astarion standing and getting dressed. They catch a glimpse of scars on his back - a sore point. The scars were carved into him by his old master. As far as Astarion knows, they're a poem, but he's never been able to read it (can't look in a mirror, after all).
- LOW_CazadorsPalace_RitualRoom_PostCombat_OM_Astarion_AOM_COM_OOM.json: Astarion addresses a defeated Cazador after their fight. He pulls his former master from the coffin where he's recovering and has to decide what to do with him - kill him or carve the scars on Astarion's back into Cazador's and then use him as a sacrifice in the ritual.

retrieved_synopses: You're in camp amid rising fear that the tadpole infection is turning party members into mind flayers — others have shown signs and tensions (Lae'zel in particular is primed to react violently). Astarion has slipped into a quiet, intimate mood (he may be tracing his scars and opening up to those he trusts) and is musing on the grim possibility of stopping a transformed companion. As a practiced killer he treats the subject with grim professional curiosity and is almost gleeful when describing methods of death, framing mercy dispatch as a "professional courtesy." He speaks lightly but seriously about the danger; if you threaten or scold him he becomes defensive and a bit sulky.

Following a trail of whispered ADs ('Psst. Over here!' 'Come on, before it's too late!') we find a pale elf, hunched down near some long grass. He insists an intellect devourer (brain monster with legs) is hiding there, trying to cajole you to look and kill it. If you approach the grass, a boar bursts out - it was a distraction while Astarion got behind you. He's on edge, but pleased to have the jump on you. He holds a blade to your throat while demanding you tell him what happened on the ship. After a mind meld (vision where he sees a glimpse of your past) you can convince him that you're both victims and should work together to find an answer. Once he realises you're not a threat his tone changes from threatening to charming.

You wake up and find Astarion hunching over you, fangs bared. You fight him off. Caught off guard, he's alarmed and worried that you're going to kill him. He tries to be charming, explaining that he's too weak without blood. If you push back against his excuses he gets frustrated - he tries to bargain with you. If you agree to let him bite you, he's thrilled. He feels in control again. After drinking, he feels invigorated and cocky.

After the goblin hunt celebration party (whether the player helped the goblins or the tieflings), Astarion has made arrangements to get intimate with the player at night. For Astarion, this is a game of power - one he's played many times before in the taverns of Baldur's Gate, trying to lure people back to his master. He's an old hand at seduction, very self-assured at first, but the player might not go along with the script he expects them to follow. The next morning, the player wakes to see Astarion standing and getting dressed. They catch a glimpse of scars on his back - a sore point. The scars were carved into him by his old master. As far as Astarion knows, they're a poem, but he's never been able to read it (can't look in a mirror, after all).

Astarion addresses a defeated Cazador after their fight. He pulls his former master from the coffin where he's recovering and has to decide what to do with him - kill him or carve the scars on Astarion's back into Cazador's and then use him as a sacrifice in the ritual.
context: The party is camped amid growing fear that the tadpole infection is turning members into mind flayers — others have shown signs and tensions are high. Astarion has slipped into a quiet, intimate mood and is musing grimly about the possibility of having to stop a transformed companion; as a practiced killer he treats the subject with professional curiosity and almost gleeful enthusiasm for different methods. He frames a mercy dispatch as a “professional courtesy” and playfully offers options, even as the topic could outrage or upset you. If you push back, threaten, or scold him, he becomes defensive and a bit sulky.
